background: ADSEP is a fully automated, “plug-and-play” multi-use single middeck locker processing facility that has been used to conduct a variety of biotechnology and life science experiments. The ADSEP facility contains three independent thermal zones, each accommodating one cassette, and an internal computer that controls the processing of all three cassettes. First, its standard 1U form factor makes it compatible with several microgravity experiment platforms aboard the ISS, including Space Tango and ICE Cubes. The complete ScienceShell hardware portfolio is fully compatible with Kiwi's ScienceBox and ScienceTaxi platforms, allowing for flexible and modular integration of experiments.

background: Spectrum supports biological experiments that demonstrate how various organisms—such as plants, microbes, and worms—develop under microgravity conditions.
name: Spectrum
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Materials ISS Experiment Flight Facility (MISSE-FF) investigated the effects of long-term exposure of materials to the space environment, including the performance, stability, and survivability of materials and components used or planned for use by NASA, commercial companies, and the Department of Defense. Over 2,000 samples have been tested by the MISSE project, including biological materials such as seeds, spores, and various types of bacteria. Each material was tested in the laboratory prior to selection and exposure, then re-tested on the ground after exposure and return. MISSE also examined crew shielding materials relevant to future Mars missions.
name: Materials ISS Experiment Flight Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED (EVA) + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: EXPOSE is a passive exposure facility flown repeatedly on the ISS; samples are exposed for multiple months. Samples are exposed to full-spectrum solar radiation or illumination, depending on the window material of each exposure cell. They are also exposed to background radiation and are either vented to space vacuum or isolated in a self-contained, sealed gaseous environment. Control samples are exposed under identical conditions except they are kept in darkness. Analysis is conducted by before-and-after comparison, requiring sample return. There are no in-situ measurement capabilities or temperature control.
data_rate: Thermal and optical sensors (no sample science data)
name: EXPOSE beyond LEO
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED (EVA) + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Biopan is a pan-shaped, retrievable exposure facility for experiments in astrobiology, chemical evolution, radiation biology, and radiation dosimetry. Externally mounted on unmanned, recoverable Foton-type satellites, Biopan completed 2-week missions in low Earth orbit (LEO) at a 63° inclination, exposing biological samples to space conditions. Six flights were completed between 1992 and 2007, with up to 10 unique experiments per flight.
name: Biopan
note_specs: Biopan carries its experiment packages (total mass 4 kg max.) on two mounting plates (total surface area 1,080 cm2).
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED (EVA) + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Gene Vault stores terrestrial specimens in deep space to provide confidence in regenerative life support architectures reliant upon plants and microorganisms. GeneVault assesses the effects of long-term exposure to space radiation on seeds, microbes, and DNA samples, which are later returned to Earth for analysis. The payload includes active and passive dosimeters.
crew_handling_required: Y, only on deployment and retrieval
crew_time: Y, only on deployment and retrieval
name: Gene Vault
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED (EVA) + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The NanoRacks External Platform (NREP) is a deploy-and-return system that exposes payloads to outer space and then retrieves them for return. It provides mechanical (mounting) and electrical interfaces outside the ISS.
name: NanoRacks External Platform
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED (EVA) + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

name: Compact TEPC

background: The plastic scintillator measures biological tissue-equivalent damage from ionizing radiation by calculating the linear energy transfer (LET) of individual particles. The polyvinyltoluene plastic scintillator provides a radiation dose response similar to that of biological tissue. Its response characteristics allow for more accurate assessment of damage from neutrons and protons in the environment.
name: Plastic Scintillators

background: The Single-Board LET Radiation Spectrometer measures the linear energy transfer (LET) spectrum of ionizing radiation events across the biologically relevant range for interplanetary space: 0.2–300 keV/µm. LET is a more accurate indicator of potential biological damage than the energy of individual particles. It also provides more meaningful insight than total ionizing dose (TID), which aggregates all ionizing radiation despite known differences in their biological effects.
name: Single-Board LET Radiation Spectrometer
note_specs: 256 bins cover 0.2 - 300 keV/µm (even spacing on log scale)
operations: FULL AUTONOMY + NO SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Advanced Biological Research System (ABRS) is a hardware system designed to conduct a wide variety of biological experiments on the International Space Station (ISS). ABRS fits within either asingle rear-breathing Space Shuttle middeck locker or an ISS EXPRESS Rack, and can support the growth of plants, microbes, and/or other small specimens by providing controlled environmental conditions.
name: Advanced Biological Research System

background: The Advanced Protein Crystallisation Facility (APCF) is a satellite-borne facility developed by the European Space Agency (ESA). The APCF first flew in space in 1993, and, since then, has been the primary facility for microgravity protein crystallisation activities in Europe. It is the predecessor to the Protein Crystallisation Diagnostics Facility (PCDF) and, from 2004, has enabled scientists to quantitatively investigate gravity-dependent effects on crystal growth.
name: Advanced Protein Crystallization Facility

background: ADSEP-2 is the second generation ADSEP, a fully automated, “plug-and-play” multi-use single middeck locker processing facility that has been used to conduct a variety of biotechnology and life science experiments. The ADSEP-2 facility contains three independent thermal zones, each accommodating one cassette, and an internal computer that controls the processing of all three cassettes. The cassettes are specifically designed for cell culturing, bioseparations, fluids processing and colloids. Each cassette is designed to provide up to 2-levels of containment for each experiment. The ADSEP Processing Facility can be operated remotely or pre-programmed to conduct each experiment cassette without requiring any scheduled crew time. ADSEP-2 has condensed electronics allowing for more experiment space than ADSEP, and can also house camera equipment.
name: ADvanced Space Experiment Processor-2

The ADSEP-4 facility contains four independent thermal zones, each accommodating one cassette, and an internal computer that controls the processing of all four cassettes. The cassettes are multipurpose for various experiment uses. Each cassette is designed to provide up to 2-levels of containment for each experiment. The ADSEP Processing Facility can be operated remotely or pre-programmed to conduct each experiment cassette without requiring any scheduled crew time. ADSEP-4 has modernized electronics and 4 cassetes, allowing for more experiments than ADSEP-2.
name: ADvanced Space Experiment Processor-4

background: The Animal Enclosure Module (AEM) is a self-contained habitat to investigate the influence of microgravity on rodent physiology and anatomy. Research conducted using AEM is analogous to the human research program, which aims to extend human presence safely beyond LEO. The International Space Station’s orbit is in LEO, at an altitude of approximately 250 miles. The AEM hardware is maintained at the Ames Research Center in Moffett Field, California by NASA.
name: Animal Enclosure Module
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Aquatic Habitat (AQH) is a self contained aquarium developed by JAXA for installation in the Japanese Experiment Module of the ISS (Kibo). It can accommodate small freshwater fish and has been utilized for the experiments to investigate how long term exposure to the microgravity and space radiation environment affects living things (including humans).

background: Astro Garden is an in-progress plant growth habitat being developed by private space company Sierra Space, sponsored by NASA. Since Astro Garden is still currently in development, not much is known about its novel features, but it is expected to be integrated with Sierra Space’s LIFE Habitat, a 3-story tall, 27-foot diameter, inflatable habitat for crewed space missions. It is intended to be used to allow for the cultivation of fresh food for astronauts, as well as study how the space environment influnces plant life.

note_specs: Water flow rate range: 0-0.5 L/min

background: The Autonomous Biological System (ABS) is a life support habitat created by Paragon Space Development Corporation that can be flown in space to provide for long term growth and breeding of aquatic plants, animals, microbes and algae. The system functions autonomously and in isolation from the spacecraft life support systems, with no mandatory crew time required for function or observation. The ABS can also be used for long term plant and animal life support and breeding on a free flyer space craft. The ABS units are a research tool for both pharmaceutical and basic space biological sciences.

background: The Bio-Analyzer detects and measures cell surface molecules on a per cell bases and assesses the soluble molecule concentration in liquid samples such as blood, saliva, or urine. It is used to get information on astronaut's biological processes without needing to send samples back to Earth. Bio-Analyzer is owned and operated by the Canadian Space Agency.
name: Bio-Analyzer
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Redwire 3D BioFabrication Facility (BFF) is the first American system capable of manufacturing human tissue in the microgravity condition of space. Utilizing adult human cells (such as pluripotent or stem cells), the system can create viable tissue in space through technology that enables it to precisely place and build ultra-fine layers of bioink
name: BioFabrication Facility

background: BIOKON provides a dedicated environment for the execution of life science experiments in microgravity. BIOKON complements effectively all types of biological Experiment Units (EU) regardless the fact that they could require electrical power or not. It is interactive with the KUBIK system.
name: BIOKON

background: The Centrifuge developed, owned, and operated by BioServe Space Technologies supports a wide variety of investigations in the life, physical, and material sciences, focusing on research on biological systems and processes. The Centrifuge is capable of holding up to 12 microcentrifuge tubes ranging in several standard sizes from 0.2 ml to 2.0 ml each or -using an exchangeable rotor- up to 16 PCR tubes (0.2 ml each) arranged in two 8-tube strips.

Once captured, the images and video can be downlinked to Earth for review by the science team allowing near-real-time feedback of the experiment. The BSMP was developed in a modular fashion allowing for new hardware to be swapped in as technology improves.
name: BioServe Microscope
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: Biotube was developed for plant gravitropic research investigating the potential for magnetic fields to orient plant roots as they grow in microgravity. Prior to flight, experimental seeds are placed into seed cassettes, that are capable of containing up to 10 seeds, and inserted between two magnets located within one of three Magnetic Field Chamber (MFC). Biotube is stored within an International Space Station (ISS) stowage locker and provides three levels of containment for chemical fixatives.

operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Boiling Experiment Facility (BXF) was designed to operate in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) on the International Space Station (ISS). The BXF consisted of a boiling chamber mounted within a containment vessel. It sought to determine the local boiling heat transfer mechanisms in microgravity for nucleate and transition boiling and critical heat flux, and to understand bubble growth, detachment and subsequent motion of single and large merged bubbles.

DECLIC is a multi-user facility developed by the French Space Agency, CNES, and flown in collaboration with NASA to support experiments on fluid physics and materials science.

The experiments are largely autonomous to minimize data transfer requirements, though the EDR can be operated remotely via telescience or in real time by the crew via a dedicated laptop.

background: Faraday is a flexible platform to fly research inside the International Space Station (ISS) or other habitats. It is economical, which promotes multiple flights versus a “one off". Faraday can support a variety of biological specimens, including shrimp, ants, and seedlings.
name: Faraday Research Facility
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Various biological samples, such as brine shrimp, ants, and plant seedlings

background: The Fluid Physics Experiment Facility investigates fluid physics phenomena in a micro-gravity environment. The FPEF consists of the core section and the mission section. The core section has observing equipment, the control equipment, and miscellaneous experiment support systems. The mission section called as the "Experiment Cell", is exchangeable according to the purpose of the experiment.
name: Fluid Physics Experiment Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Analytical Cassette Transfer Tool (ACT2) is a low-cost, disposable device that efficiently transfers experiment samples in a safe and contained manner from unique experiment specific spaceflight hardware to on-orbit analytical tools that enable real-time analysis in microgravity. ACT interfaces with several flight qualified processing payloads to extract experiment samples via a needle-less septum and then allows transfer of those samples into a number of different on-orbit analytical devices, including such instrumentation as the Light Microscopy Module, the Microfluidic Flow Cytometer, a Spectrophotometer, and/or a Mass Spectrometer.
name: Analytical Containment Transfer Tool
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Fluid Science Laboratory is a European (ESA's) science payload designed for use in Columbus built by Alenia Spazio, OHB-System and Verhaert Design and Development.[1] It is a multi-user facility for conducting fluid physics research in microgravity conditions.
name: Fluid Science Laboratory
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Fluids Integrated Rack (FIR), located in the U.S. Laboratory Module (Destiny) accommodates experiments that address critical space exploration research and technology needs for advanced life support (i.e., air revitalization, water reclamation, etc.), power, propulsion, and spacecraft thermal control systems. The primary focus of these experiments involves boiling heat transfer, multiphase flow, liquid vapor interface control, and liquid and vapor evaporation and condensation.
name: Fluids Integrated Rack - Fluids and Combustion Facility
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Fruit Fly Lab is a platform on the ISS that enables long-duration fruit fly (Drosophila Melanogaster) experiments in space. These investigations study how exposure to microgravity and the other attributes of the space environment affect fruit flies, providing valuable information for long-term spaceflight and response to illness.
name: Fruit Fly Lab; Fruit Fly Lab Experiment Hardware
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: 15 vials per cassette, 12 cassettes per rack

background: Granada Crystallisation Facility (GCF) is a crystallisation device designed to perform counter-diffusion experiments. GCF allows one to explore and exploit the coupling between crystallisation and diffusion. The role of viscous fluids, gels and/or microgravity can be enhanced by using capillary volumes, creating a perfect diffusive mass transport scenario.
name: Granada Crystallization Facility
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: Hermes is a research facility on the ISS aimed at regolith and granular material investigations with applications to asteroids, planetary science, and exploration. Hermes is a reconfigurable on-orbit facility capable of accommodating up to four user-configurable experiment volumes at a time. The facility provides long duration exposure to microgravity and vacuum. The facility is open to small experiments that can fit within the Hermes volume and interface requirements.
name: Hermes Facility
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The ISS SERVIR Environmental Research and Visualization System (ISERV) was an automated system designed to acquire over 40,000 images of the Earth's surface from February 2013 to December 2014. The goal was to improve automatic image capturing and data transfer. The images taken will help environmental scientists, disaster responders and other Earth-based users.
name: ISS SERVIR Environmental Research and Visualization System
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: JEM-EF is a unique platform on the ISS that is located outside of the Pressurized Module and is continuously exposed to the space environment. Astronauts exchange experiment payloads or hardware from the Pressurized Module through the scientific airlock using the Kibo Remote Manipulator System. Items positioned on the exterior platform focus on Earth observation as well as communication, scientific, engineering and materials science experiments.
name: Japanese Experiment Module - Exposed Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: 12 total EEU's, ~0.8 m x 1.0 m x1.85 m, <500 kg per unit

background: JAXA Mouse Habitat Unit examines the effects of partial G on mice using the JAXA-developed mouse habitat cage units (HCU) on the ISS. Mice are exposed to 4 different gravity conditions on independent centrifuges: uG, 0.33G, 0.66G, 1G.
name: JAXA Mouse Habitat Unit
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The KEyence Research MIcroscope Testbed performs fluorescence, brightfield, and phase-contrast imaging on a variety of specimen holders without the need for a darkroom. It includes a fully motorized, six-objective lens revolver, motorized stage, electronically controlled filter turret, built-in sample enclosure, and a 12 bit camera that can switch between monochrome and color imaging.
name: KEyence Research MIcroscope Testbed
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

name: KOBAIRO Rack
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The Life Sciences Glovebox (LSG) is an enclosed work area that accommodates research in a “workbench”-type environment. Two crew members can work in the LSG at the same time. The enclosed working volume is held at negative pressure relative to the crew living area. The LSG is a level of containment, and experiments are designed to attach such that there is no exchange of biological matter between the cabin and the LSG.
name: Life Sciences Glovebox
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Light Microscopy Module (LMM) is a remotely controllable, automated, on-orbit microscope subrack facility, allowing flexible scheduling and control of fluids and biology experiments within the Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF) and Fluids Integrated Rack (FIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).
name: Light Microscopy Module
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Materials Science Laboratory (MSL) is a payload on board the ISS for materials science experiments in low gravity. It is installed in NASA's MSRR, which is placed in the Destiny laboratory on board the ISS. Its purpose is to process material samples in different ways: directional solidification of metals and alloys, crystal growth of semi-conducting materials, thermo-physical properties and diffusion experiments of alloys and glass-forming materials, and investigations on polymers and ceramics at the liquid-solid phase transition.
name: Materials Science Laboratory
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: up to 12 sample cartrages per batch
specimen_types_supported: Metals, alloys, ceramics, semiconductors, glass-formers, polymers

background: The Materials Science Research Rack-1 is the hosting infrastructre used for basic materials research on the ISS. It primarily houses the MSL research payload, but can support other equipment. Several material groups can be studied, including metals, alloys, polymers, semiconductors, ceramics, and glasses.
name: Materials Science Research Rack-1
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: the Mice Drawer System (MDS) is a reseach payload that houses 6 mice per mission. It was designed to function autonomously for more than 3 months and to involve crew only for maintenance activities. It holds the record for the longest continuous mouse research experiment in space, at 91 days.
name: Mice Drawer System Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: Microgravity Experiment Research Locker/Incubator is a thermal carrier that provides a thermally controlled environment for scientific experiments between -20°C and 48.5°C in the International Space Station EXPRESS Rack.
name: Microgravity Experiment Research Locker Incubator
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) is a sealed facility that provides an enclosed space for investigations to be conducted on the ISS The MSG accommodates small- and medium-sized investigations from disciplines including biotechnology, combustion science, fluid physics, fundamental physics, and materials science. The MSG can provide experiments with power, data acquisition, computer communications, vacuum, nitrogen, and specialized tools.
name: Microgravity Science Glovebox
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Microgravity Vibration Isolatiion System (MVIS) is a six degrees of freedom magnetic isolation system that isolates Fluid Science Laboratory (FSL) Experiment Containers from the vibrations of the ISS. It is integrated with the FSL on the ISS and uses magnetism to "float" the experiment containers without contacting the ISS.
name: Microgravity Vibration Isolation Subsystem
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Microgravity-based Automated Manufacturing and Bioprocessing Outpost (Mambo), designed by Space Tango, is designed to host multiple microgravity experiments and in-space manufacturing payloads. Each payload is attached to a Mambo Tray that slides into the Mambo facility. A new tray can be installed at the end of each experiment cycle, allowing multiple researchers to use the facility during a single mission.
name: Microgravity-based Automated Manufacturing and Bioprocessing Outpost
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: MicroPREP is Canadian lab-on-a-chip technology that is based on centrifugal microfluidics with pneumatic control and uses smartphone-sized microfluidic chips. From a sample of body fluids, MicroPREP technology can isolate multiple macro-molecules such as DNA and proteins, or rare cells, making it possible to assess immune system state, inflammation, bone loss or radiation effects.
name: MicroPREP
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Body fluids such as blood, urine, saliva

background: Mochii™ is a field-portable, high-resolution imager and spectrometer. Mochii was designed as a new class of analyzer to provide some never-before-available capabilities. Mochii combines the best of both light and electron microscopes in the size of a coffee maker.
name: Mochii
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Suitable for biological, material, chemical, and more samples

background: Multi Purpose Small payload Rack (MSPR) has 2 workspaces and a work table: Work Volume (WV), Work Bench (WB) and Small Experiment Area (SEA). They can be used almost like a laboratory on the ground, storing equipment freely and easily, using general interfaces of power supplies, communication, and videos. MSPR can be used for many applications, including science and educational missions.
interface_definitions: ExPRESS Rack Compatible. WV + WB combined: Up to ~500 W (28 VDC: 380 W; 16 VDC: 95 W; 12 VDC: 95 W) SEA: Up to ~95 W (12 VDC).
name: Multi Purpose Small Payload Rack
note_specs: As a developing instrument, these are likely to change
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: Multi Purpose Small payload Rack-2 (MSPR-2) is the second generation MSPR that has a Work Volume (WV). For this genearation, the Small Experiment Area (SEA) and Work Bench (WB) were omitted. The MSPR-2 simplifies the configuration and is primarily intended to host larger, standalone payloads that are autonomous, streamlining operation at the cost of reduced versatility.
name: Multi Purpose Small Payload Rack-2
note_specs: Up to 5,000 time magnification, accelerating voltage 10kV
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: MOBIAS is a modular bioreactor system developed by BioServe Space Technologies to enable automated microbial culture and sampling under microgravity conditions. It uses long, thin gas-permeable bags and automated fluid exchange to support diffusion-based bioprocessing without agitation mechanisms. MOBIAS was never used outside of the CGBA incubator.
compatibility_on_orbit_sample_processing: Partial (extra specimen analysis done after sample return to Earth)
name: Modular Orbital Bioreactor with Automated Sampling
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The NanoRacks–Astrium Centrifuge delivers a commercial onboard centrifuge facility aboard the ISS. Installed within NanoRacks Platform‑3, it enables researchers to perform gravity-controlled biological, materials, and fluid experiments in orbit, simulating microgravity to 1 g (or Mars/Moon scale) while using standard NanoRacks biological containers.
name: NanoRacks Astrium Centrifuge
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED

background: The NanoRacks Microscopes facility is a commercial onboard imaging platform aboard the ISS, offering two optical microscopes (reflective and transmitted light) in plug-and-play USB-compatible form. It provides crew-accessible magnification tools (5×, 10×, 20×) with direct USB data capture for in-situ sample imaging anywhere on the Station.
name: NanoRacks Microscopes
note_specs: MOBIAS does not have its own temperature control; was always uses inside CGBA incubator
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

autonomy: Y; 30-60 min per set of trials
background: The NanoRacks Plate Reader‑2 is a fully‑functional SpectraMax M5e multi‑mode microplate reader - the first such instrument in space - deployed aboard the ISS under NanoRacks' commercial service agreement. It allows researchers to perform absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, and polarization assays on 6‑ to 384‑well microplates on-orbit, including thermal regulation for long-duration biochemical experiments.
name: NanoRacks Plate Reader
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Plant seeds, microbes, tissues, small invertebrates, cell cultures, crystallization droplets

background: Pore Formation and Mobility Investigation Facility is a materials science experiment platform—specifically a translational Bridgman-style furnace inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox—designed to study how bubbles form and move during directional solidification of transparent analog metals (e.g. succinonitrile) in microgravity, to improve understanding of pore-related defects in space and terrestrial manufacturing.
name: Pore Formation and Mobility Investigation Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Cells, microbial cultures, plant tissues, fluid physics samples, small lab-on-a-chip platforms

background: The Protein Crystal Growth - Single Locker Thermal Enclosure System (PCG-STES) is an ISS-ready, temperature‑controlled enclosure occupying one middeck locker–equivalent (one MLE) in an EXPRESS rack. It houses protein crystallization hardware such as PCAM, and maintains precise incubation temperatures (±0.5 °C), enabling microgravity crystallization of proteins with vapor or diffusion methods.
interface_definitions: Conductive thermal interface through side walls; power and data bus for housed crystallization hardware
measurements: Temperature logged; image/video capture of crystals via camera in PCAM/DCAM units
name: Protein Crystal Growth - Single Locker Thermal Enclosure System
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Yes—environment monitored by STES thermal system (temperature)
volume: One EXPRESS rack slot (1 MLE) accommodating PCAM or DCAM trays

background: The Protein Crystallization Research Facility (PCRF) is installed within Kibo’s Ryutai Rack and supports high-quality protein crystal growth experiments in microgravity using motor-driven cell cartridges with precise temperature control and real-time imaging. Since 2009, it has enabled structural biology breakthroughs in drug discovery and molecular research.
dims: PCRF Rack housing six Cell Cartridges; each cartridge ≈ 15 × 10 × 7 cm
interface_definitions: Each cartridge: thermistors (2), Peltier module (1), motor (1), photo sensor (1); CCD camera (1/2‑inch), LED lighting, data/power bus to Rack
measurements: Continuous CCD imaging of crystal growth; motorized mixing; environment logged
microscopy: Y; Imaging resolution >40 µm per pixel (CCD spec)
name: Protein Crystallization Research Facility
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Sample tubes ~1 cm radius, ~30 cm length
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Thermistors inside each cartridge monitor temperature
volume: One rack slot in Ryutai Rack

background: The BioMole Facility is a molecular biology instrument developed by NASA’s Crew Health Care Systems (CHeCS) program for the ISS. It enables on-orbit DNA sequencing using portable, miniaturized devices like Oxford Nanopore’s MinION. This removes the need for culturing microbes or returning samples to Earth, allowing real-time microbial monitoring of the station environment to support astronaut health and mission safety.
name: Research Integration Office (RIO) BioMole Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: PCAM: up to 6 cylinders per STES, each cylinder houses 63 wells (~40 µl each); total up to ~378 experiments per STES
specimen_types_supported: Protein solutions in crystallization trays (e.g., PCAM trays)

background: The Ring Sheared Drop (RSD) system is a containerless biochemical reactor flown aboard the ISS since July 2019. Mounted in the Microgravity Science Glovebox, it supports the study of protein fluid dynamics—especially amyloid fibril formation—without interference from container walls. This facilitates research in neurodegenerative disease and pharmaceutical processing under microgravity conditions.
imaging: Y; microscope (10×), high-frame-rate video & still cameras
interface_definitions: Bolted to MSG floor; power/data via MSG; USB to onboard camera/computer systems
measurements: Real-time video and still imaging; turbidity measurement; flow analysis via tracer particles
name: Ring Sheared Drop
note_specs: One Ryutai Rack holds ~6 cartridges with up to 144 protein wells total.
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Six cartridges × 10‑16 wells per cartridge; 10–500 µL volume per well
specimen_types_supported: Purified protein solutions (single proteins or protein–drug complexes) in >10 µL volumes per well
temperature_range: Independently controlled 0–35 °C per cartridge via Peltier control

background: The Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction (SoFIE) payload is installed in the ISS’s Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR). It enables multiple investigations into how solid materials ignite, burn, and go out under microgravity conditions, variable oxygen, pressure, and flow rates. These experiments inform spacecraft material selection and fire safety protocols for future exploration missions to the Moon or Mars.
interface_definitions: Integrated into CIR Standard Rack Interfaces; uses CIR systems
measurements: Flame Spread Rate, Extinction Limits, Video Diagnostics, Radiometry, Flow Data
name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Swab samples; small-volume DNA prep kits (~100–200 µL scale)
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Sensors in CIR environment manage gas, flow, pressure, radiometry

background: The Solidification Using a Baffle in Sealed Ampoules (SUBSA) aboard the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) performs gradient freeze solidification of semiconductor and scintillator crystals using sealed ampoules with built-in baffles to minimize melt convection in microgravity. This setup enables in‑situ crystal growth monitoring via high-definition video and thermal control, improving our understanding of materials science under near‑nanog acceleration conditions.
heat_sink: Y; Cold plate connection to MSG cold sink
interface_definitions: Connected to MSG utilities: power, data, video; uses MSG cold‐plate sink; remote commanding via MSG interface
measurements: Real-time HD video (zoom/focus/rate control), four thermocouples for thermal profiling with overlay on video feed
name: Solidification Using a Baffle in Sealed Ampoules (SUBSA)
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Up to 12 mL per syringe; drop pinned ~25.4 mm diameter
specimen_types_supported: Protein solutions (e.g., human/bovine serum albumin); tracer particles

background: The Solution Crystallization Observation Facility (SCOF) is part of JAXA’s Solution/Protein Crystal Growth Facility aboard Kibo (the Ryutai rack). It’s designed for real-time, multi-modal observation of solution crystal growth under microgravity, using high-precision interferometry and microscopy. It enables measurement of temperature, concentration, and crystal morphology over time, aiding materials science, biophysics, and pharmaceutical research.
category: Physical Science – Materials Science / Thermodynamic Analysis
gas_control: Y; O2 concentration, pressure, and flow speed controlled by CIR
heat_sink: Y; Peltier cooling is linked to thermal paths within Ryutai rack
measurements: Mach‑Zehnder interference, Michelson interferometer, amplitude-modulation, polarized, bright‑field microscopes; dynamic light scattering, fluorescence decay, and spectrophotometry options
name: Solution Crystallization Observation Facility
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Various Geometries; Include flat sheets, cylinders, spheres (~4–30 cm length or ~5 cm sphere)
specimen_types_supported: Solid combustible materials: plexiglass (PMMA), cotton fabrics, coated surfaces, cylinders, sheets, spheres
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Thermistor or thermocouple for temperature; pressure and gas sensors per pressure system.
volume: Approx middeck locker size; fits into EXPRESS rack (1 Standard Locker)

background: The Space Automated Lab Incubator (SALI), developed by BioServe Space Technologies, is a compact, dual-mode incubator/freezer deployed aboard ISS middeck locker-equivalent racks. It provides controlled thermal environments from –20 °C to +48 °C for various biological, life‑science, and materials experiments. SALI offers minimal crew interaction with remote monitoring and full rack-compatibility, serving as a flexible incubator/freezer for advanced payloads.
dims: Internal volume > 24 L; internal dimensions ~17.25″ × 11.10″ × 7.75″ (~43.8 cm × 28.2 cm × 19.7 cm)
gas_control: Ambient Air in MSG (no controlled gas environment)
measurements: Temperature logging, chamber status; optional instrumentation via inserts
name: Space Automated Lab Incubator
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
power: Operates Off Rack 28 V DC Line
specimen_size: Ampoules: 16 mm diameter, up to 290 mm length; hot zone ~200 mm, transparent observation zone ~95 mm
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Internal temperature sensors; humidity and gas not monitored unless via insert
temperature_range: Up to 850 °C in furnace hot zone; ambient at transparent zone and cold sink (~22 °C)
volume: Approx middeck locker size; fits into EXPRESS rack (1 Standard Locker)

background: The TELe-Luminescence Analysis System (TELLAS) was deployed aboard ISS’s Kibo module in June 2021, and is the first space-borne bioluminescence imaging instrument for in-vivo monitoring of gene expression in small animals (e.g., mice). It enables researchers to remotely observe biological processes, such as aging-related gene activation, without returning samples to Earth.
measurements: 2D luminescence imaging (fixed FOV 100 × 100 mm), no fluorescence/CT/X‑ray modes
name: TELe-Luminescence Analysis System
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Standard cartridge: 220 mm diameter × 65 mm height; cell volume varies per design.

background: The Wet Lab Kit is a soft-goods caddy developed by NASA (Wyle Laboratories) and available via the ISS National Lab. It provides generic consumables and tools (e.g., syringes, vials, gloves, swabs, absorbent pads, syringe loaders) that support sample collection and preparation for life-science experiments in microgravity. It functions as a modular “lab pantry” to support payload operations without needing dedicated hard hardware modules.
category: Life Sciences – Sample Handling Consumables / Support Kit
name: Wet Lab Kit
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
volume: Soft‑goods bag sized to fit ISS middeck locker or cargo vehicle stowage

background: The Wet Lab RNA SmartCycler is the thermal cycler (Cepheid SmartCycler) module within NASA’s WetLab‑2 system aboard the ISS. It enables real-time, quantitative RT‑qPCR gene expression analysis in orbit using crew-prepared RNA samples. This facility supports investigations into crew health, microbial monitoring, cell stress responses, and environmental gene detection without requiring sample return to Earth.
category: Life Sciences - DNA/RNA Analysis, Molecular Biology
data_rate: Low  - qPCR output data downlinked via ISS communication
interface_definitions: Connected to rack power, data interface; samples loaded manually into tubes; control via rack interface or ground uplink
measurements: Real-time fluorescence signal; S-curve output; data multiplexed to up to 4 probes per tube
name: Wet Lab RNA SmartCycler
note_specs: Requires installation by crew; Specifically Observation Cartridge and Calibrtion Light Source
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED

background: The Aquatic Habitat (AQH) is a life-science payload installed in JAXA’s Kibo module aboard the ISS. It enables long-duration (up to ~90 days) microgravity experiments with freshwater fish such as medaka or zebrafish. The system supports multigenerational studies, environmental monitoring, feeding control, and noninvasive CCD-based observation.
imaging: Y; CCD + IR cameras per aquarium
name: Aquatic Research Facility
note_specs: This is a manual consumable; There is no electronic/power interfaces
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Kit contents include vials, syringes, needles, gloves, absorbent pads; flexible per experiment needs
specimen_types_supported: Broad range: blood, saliva, urine, tissue samples, microbial cultures, plant samples, environmental swab
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Yes – multiple sensors monitor environmental variables within the water loop.
volume: One small rack locker within Kibo module

background: The Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) is NASA’s most advanced plant growth system aboard the ISS. Installed in EXPRESS Rack and ISIS drawer, it supports fully automated, closed-loop plant cultivation experiments lasting up to ~135 days. APH maintains controlled CO₂, lighting, temperature, humidity, nutrient delivery, and monitoring—ideal for studying plant physiology, microbial interactions, and plant-based life support systems in microgravity.
category: Life Sciences - Plant Growth / Environmental Control
dims: Quad-locker payload + ISIS drawer (~fits EXPRESS rack lower half)
experiment_duration: Sample prep ~25 min; run up to ~4 hours; total cycle less than ~3 hours from RNA extraction to data available
name: Plant Growth Unit
operational_temperature: Shoot zone: 18 °C–30 °C ±0.5 °C; uniformity ±1 °C between canopy and rack
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: 16 reaction tubes per run; fluid volume typically µL-scale (e.g., purified RNA ~10–50 µL)
specimen_types_supported: RNA from microbial cultures, tissues, environmental swabs, clinical samples
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Yes – comprehensive set (>180 calibrated sensors) monitoring environment and plant canopy

background: The Animal Access Unit (AAU) is a transfer interface within NASA’s Rodent Research Hardware System. It enables safe, contained movement of mice between the Transporter (launch vehicle module) and the long-term Habitat Unit aboard ISS, and back into the Transporter for return or further transfer. It maintains containment of waste and bedding during animal transfer steps.
category: Life Sciences - Animal Habitat Support / Logistics Interface
gas_control: Y; O₂ supply / CO₂ removal via gas-permeable membrane “artificial lung” system
interface_definitions: Mechanical interface to Transporter and Habitat
name: Animal Access Unit
note_specs: JAXA payload rack interfaces: power, data; remote control of feeding, lighting via crew/ground command
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN NOT REQUIRED
specimen_size: Two aquaria, each ~0.7 L capacity; total ~3.2 L water volume
volume: Interface unit to mate Animal Transporter and Habitat, minimal free volume

background: BRIC‑Opti is a variant within NASA’s Biological Research in Canisters (BRIC) suite, designed to support passive microbial and plant tissue culture in sealed OptiCell™ chambers under a controlled initial atmosphere. It enables closed-environment biological experiments with onboard autonomy and minimal crew interaction in microgravity.
category: Life Sciences – Culturing, Growth, Microbiology / Environmental Monitoring
gas_control: CO₂ control: 400 ppm up to 5,000 ppm ±50 ppm; O₂ and atmosphere regulated via internal airflow management
name: BRIC-Opti
note_specs: For Interface: crew watering refill station and remote ground commands supported; For Heat Sync: uses thermoelectric cooling/heating internally; connected to rack thermal system
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Shoot area ~1,708 cm²; shoot height up to 43 cm; root area ~1,853 cm²; root depth ~5 cm
specimen_types_supported: Arabidopsis, dwarf wheat, lettuce, peppers and other crops. Supports plant–microbe co-culture, algae, and root zone studies

background: The Biopack facility was developed by ESA (European Space Agency) as a compact, middeck locker–mounted biological payload platform for the Space Shuttle and eventually the ISS/Columbus module. It includes an incubator (with centrifuge), cooler, and freezer, allowing experiments on plant tissue, microbes, insects, or cell cultures across varying gravity levels by running on-orbit or via centrifuge exposure. Designed for multi-user, high containment biological research in microgravity or artificial gravity up to 2×g.
category: Life Sciences - Culturing, Growth, Microbiology / Exposure Facilities
compatibility_on_orbit_sample_processing: Partial (extra specimen analysis done after sample return to Earth)
dims: Fits within ESA Type‑I/E and Type‑II/E locker frames (middeck or EDR drawer size) – approximate middeck locker volume (~25 × 35 × 50 cm)
experiment_duration: Transfer occurs during experiment start and end—habitat durations up to ~90 day
heat_sink: Y; through BIF air interfaces and heat exhaust systems
interface_definitions: Biopack Interface Frame (BIF) connects BEI to spacecraft
measurements: BEI computer logs basic temperature and centrifuge run data; no microscopy or imaging onboard
name: Biopack
note_specs: For Interface: manual crew interfacing must occur for mouse transfer; no electrical/power/data connection
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Up to 20 mice in Transporter; 5–10 mice per Habitat side; AAU accommodates transfers of up to that capacity
volume: Single middeck locker or equivalent EDR drawer

background: The AEM‑X (Animal Enclosure Module‑X) is an upgraded rodent habitat module used for long‑duration (up to 90 days) experiments aboard the ISS. It supports up to 10 adult mice, integrating environmental telemetry sensors and a camera system, enabling real-time remote monitoring and physiological data collection through the NASA Rodent Research Facility.
measurements: Temperature, humidity, CO₂, air flow; video (visible and IR) monitoring
name: Rodent Habitat (AEM-X) ; Rodent Research Facility
note_specs: BRIC‑Opti is designed for microbial/plant tissue culturing under defined gas conditions; it does not support molecular, genomic, or metabolic assays onboard.
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Microbes; plant tissue cultures; cell cultures in OptiCell™ plates

background: The BioRack is a NanoRacks-provided, ESA‑heritage experimental facility installed in the Kibo module on the ISS. It supports contained, multi-user biological investigations, offering temperature-controlled incubation, simulated gravity via centrifuge, and specimen handling within a glovebox-like interface. It enables studies on microbes, cells, small plants, and tissues under varying gravity (Earth-, Moon-, Mars‑like) conditions with remote operations.
category: Life Sciences – Culturing, Growth, Microbiology / Exposure Facilities
heat_sink: Y; for centrifuge and heat removal via rack airflow and thermal control cabling
name: BioRack
note_specs: This instrument was originally developed for STS‑107 and early ISS assembly era but was never fully deployed operationally on ISS; activity ceased post‑Shuttle era. It had no operational flight; development in early 2000s; planned for STS‑107 mission pre‑2003 (development canceled after Columbia accident)
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Standard ESA ECs (Type I/II) holding small culture units
specimen_types_supported: Mammalian cell and tissue cultures, small plants, insects, microbial samples

background: The Cell Culture Model (CCM) consists of JAXA’s Cell Experiment Units (CEU & CEU2) and Microbial Experiment Units (MEU/V‑MEU) housed within the Cell Biology Experiment Facility (CBEF) on ISS Kibo. These automated culture units support cell and microbial life science experiments under controlled microgravity and artificial gravity (via turntable), offering environmental control (temperature, humidity, CO₂), automated media exchange, sampling/fixation, and onboard imaging.
category: Life Sciences – Culturing, Growth, Microbiology / Cell Culture
mass: CEU: ~2.5 kg; CEU2: ~5.6 kg; MEU: ~2.5 kg
measurements: Temperature/humidity sensors; CEU2: CCD imaging with laser illumination; fluidic logs; CEU supports fixation sampling units
name: Cell Culture Model
operational_temperature: CEU: 37 °C ± 1 °C; CEU2: 24 °C ± 1 °C; MEU ambient monitored range
operations: NO CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
volume: One canister per BEU slot in CBEF turntable

background: The Aquatic Animal Experiment Unit (AAEU) is NASDA/JAXA’s historic aquatic biology facility developed for Space Shuttle‐based life sciences on Spacelab missions (e.g. IML‐2, STS‑65). It supported experiments with small aquatic animals—such as medaka fish, newts, oyster toadfish—including life-cycle and neuro‑behavioral studies in microgravity using autonomous water control, feeding, gas exchange, lighting, and video observation.
category: Life Sciences – Animal Habitat (Aquatic Animal Experiment Unit) / Environmental Monitoring
name: Aquatic Animal Experiment Unit
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: Experiment containers inserted into cassettes; small sample volumes in sealed EC carriers
specimen_types_supported: Bacteria, fungi, cell cultures, small plants, tissues, microbial biofilms
temp_gas_rh_sensors: Flow and temperature sensors present; water quality via filter system; biological filter monitors ammonia/nitrite levels

background: The Frog Environmental Unit (FEU) was part of the Spacelab‑J mission (STS‑47, 1992), designed for amphibian reproductive biology experiments in microgravity. It enabled timed hormone-induced ovulation and fertilization of adult Xenopus laevis, incubation of eggs and embryos under both microgravity and simulated 1 g (via an internal centrifuge), then transfer for crew fixation and observation.
category: Life Sciences - Culturing, Growth, Animal Habitat
dims: Approx cylindrical canister ~457 mm diameter × 457 mm length
interface_definitions: Internal centrifuge, liquid and gas loop life‑support; connection to GPWS glovebox for manipulations
measurements: ECG, vestibular nerve telemetry; video observation; microscopy via GPWS dissecting microscope
name: Frog Environmental Unit
note_specs: Pumps and fluidics require thermal control via BEU/CBEF interfaces.
operational_temperature: Maintained ~60 °F (~15 °C); water loop had heating control
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_size: CEU: two chambers (3 ml & 9 ml media; 10 cm² & 30 cm² areas); CEU2: two micro‑chambers (3 × 3 × 60 mm) with sampling units; MEU: up to six T‑25 flask volume (~1.3 L)
specimen_types_supported: Mammalian cell lines, microbial cultures, floating organisms (e.g., planktonic species)

background: The Closed Equilibriated Biological Aquatic System (CEBAS) is a modular closed-loop aquatic ecosystem developed for multi-species long-duration life‑science experiments in microgravity, designed to operate as a self‑sustaining aquatic bioregenerative system. It integrates fish, snails, plants, and microbes within a controlled aquatic loop regulated by environmental sensors and automated life‑support controls. Tested terrestrially and via short spaceflight missions.
category: Life Sciences – Animal–Plant Aquatic Ecosystem / Environmental Monitoring
gas_control: Gas-exchange via “artificial lung” membrane; oxygen/CO₂ dissolved gas exchange built into flow circuit
interface_definitions: Electronics module for data acquisition/control; integrated flow, lighting, temperature control; manual loading of biological components into housing cassette
name: Closed Equilibrated Biological Aquatic System
note_specs: Predecessor to ISS Aquatic Research Facility (AQH)
operations: CREW TIME REQUIRED + SAMPLE RETURN REQUIRED
specimen_types_supported: Medaka (Oryzias latipes), goldfish, Japanese newt (Cynops pyrrhogaster), oyster toadfish; eggs and larvae in cassettes
volume: internal volumes ~100 L animal + two 15 L plant tanks + filters (~6 L total)
